title: Nangaa Says Doha Process 'Not Dead,' Accuses Tshisekedi of Stalling
detail: AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa said Sept 2 that the Doha-mediated peace process is "not dead" despite persistent disagreements with Kinshasa, and that his delegation had responded to a request President Tshisekedi made via Qatar after the fall of Goma and Bukavu to open discussions. Nangaa nonetheless accused the government of using the Doha track to "gagner du temps" (buy time) rather than negotiate in good faith, declaring "Le problème au Congo, c'est monsieur Tshisekedi" ("The problem in Congo is Mr. Tshisekedi") and criticizing simultaneous FARDC arrest operations during prisoner-release discussions as "aberrant." He said his camp remains committed to a negotiated outcome despite the rhetoric. The remarks came as the AFC/M23 side continues to debate whether to join Tshisekedi's separate national dialogue, which the government has said armed-group leaders cannot automatically join.

confidenceReason: Nangaa's remarks are corroborated by two independent Congolese outlets covering the same statements; the political accusations against Tshisekedi are Nangaa's own characterization, not independently verified fact.

title: UN's Swan and Huang Xia Meet Kagame in Kigali on Eastern DRC Security Ahead of MONUSCO Mandate Review
detail: MONUSCO chief James Swan, who succeeded Bintou Keita in April 2026, and UN Special Envoy for the Great Lakes Huang Xia met Rwandan President Paul Kagame in Kigali on Sept 2 as part of a regional tour that also stopped in Burundi and Uganda, a day after the two envoys met Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe. Rwanda's presidency said discussions focused on "the necessity of addressing the deep-rooted causes of conflict" in eastern DRC and its security impact on Rwanda. The visit came amid friction between Kigali and MONUSCO over FDLR repatriation verification: Nduhungirehe said 81 people MONUSCO had repatriated to Rwanda as ex-FDLR combatants were later found to be Congolese civilians with no Rwandan origin. Swan is due to brief the UN Security Council in the run-up to MONUSCO's mandate renewal in December 2026.

media.caption: UN MONUSCO chief James Swan and Great Lakes envoy Huang Xia meet Rwandan President Paul Kagame in Kigali, Sept 2, 2026

confidenceReason: The meeting and its stated agenda are corroborated by two independent Congolese outlets and confirmed via Rwandan Foreign Minister Nduhungirehe's own social media post; the disputed 81-person FDLR repatriation claim is Rwanda's characterization, not independently verified.

title: DRC Ebola Death Toll Passes 3,000 as Confirmed Cases Reach 6,186
detail: DRC's Institut National de Santé Publique reported Sept 2 that the Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak had passed 3,000 deaths for the first time — 3,007 deaths among 6,186 confirmed cases (case fatality rate 48.6%), with 1,409 recoveries. The milestone came days after the outbreak topped 6,000 confirmed cases on Aug 31, reinforcing its status as DRC's largest and deadliest Ebola epidemic on record, ahead of the 2018-2020 outbreak's 3,317 cases, and the second-deadliest globally after the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic. The outbreak, declared a public health emergency in mid-May in Ituri, continues to spread across six provinces amid insecurity, displacement and a still-unapproved vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain.
